opensmart/.description: The whole application. Renamed from OpenSMART/ to opensmart/ (all-lowercase convention).
opensmart/.backend/: FastAPI app (opensmart/backend/app/), pyproject.toml, uv.lock, requirements.txt fallback.
opensmart/.scripts/: App launcher scripts: run_app.sh, dev_backend.sh, dev_frontend.sh, reset_telemetry_db.sh.
opensmart/.containers/run/: Moved here from the repo-root containers/run/, so the app container's host-path-parity mount (see deployment.phases phase 4) covers it. Per-tool docker-compose.yml + bind-mounted volumes/data/ (never named Docker volumes): opensearch, arkime, suricata, zeek, wireguard, openvpn, wazuh, opensmart, plus vpn/<instance>/ compose projects generated at runtime by backend/app/vpn.py. nginx/ is the tools front-door reverse proxy (serves the app + tool aliases /arkime /wazuh /proxmox /opnsense from one origin on :8080; started by opensmart.sh _start_front_proxy). Started/stopped by backend/app/provisioning.py (and vpn.py) through the docker-socket-proxy sidecar, not by the operator directly.

containers/.description: Docker deployment tooling. Renamed from Containers/ to containers/. Only build/ and OpenSMART-Standalone/ live here now — run/ moved to opensmart/containers/run/ (see the opensmart/ entry above).
containers/.OpenSMART-Standalone/: Reference Docker Compose bundle (network-sensor stack: Suricata, Zeek, Arkime, OpenSearch, WireGuard, OpenVPN, nginx). Standalone reference tool, run manually via its own deploy.sh, independent of opensmart.sh. Keeps its original mixed-case directory name.
containers/.build/: Per-tool Dockerfiles used by 'opensmart.sh install': base, suricata, zeek, wireguard, openvpn, opensmart. Official upstream images (OpenSearch, Arkime, nginx) have no local Dockerfile. Stays at the repo root — these are build-time templates, not tied to a running instance.

layout.docs/: Human-readable documentation (this directory) plus this MANIFEST.json.
layout.scripts/: Repo-root complementary scripts not tied to the app or the container builders (currently: opensmart-eve-collector.service, a systemd unit template).
layout.logs/: Centralized runtime log directory (gitignored contents, tracked .gitkeep).

start.container_exists_behavior: --bind/--prod are ignored (printed note explains why). Starts the container if not already running (docker compose start), then runs the shared integrity check (see integrity_check below).
start.no_container_behavior: Runs opensmart/scripts/run_app.sh start --host ADDRESS --port PORT [--prod] directly on the host. --bind defaults to 0.0.0.0:8000 when omitted.
start.dev_mode: Runs uvicorn (--reload) on the given bind address/port plus the Vite dev server on :5173. Blocks on Enter to reveal the first-run admin password.
start.prod_mode: Builds the frontend once (npm run build) instead of starting the Vite dev server, serves it from FastAPI via a StaticFiles mount, and skips the interactive password-reveal prompt (prints it non-interactively). This is the mode the container entrypoint uses.

restart.action: docker compose restart in opensmart/containers/run/opensmart/, then the shared integrity check. Errors clearly if no container exists yet.

recreate.action: Prompts for confirmation (must type RECREATE) if a container already exists, then docker compose rm -f -s (container only, not the image/network/bind-mounted app data), rebuilds the opensmart/web image from the current source/Dockerfile (docker build, normal layer caching), then docker compose up -d, then the shared integrity check. Skips the confirmation if no container exists yet. The rebuild step ensures recreate no longer reuses whatever image was already tagged opensmart/web after a git pull brings in Dockerfile changes.

uninstall.action: Prompts for confirmation (must type UNINSTALL), then runs `docker compose down` in every opensmart/containers/run/*/ directory that has a docker-compose.yml (main app + proxy, and any tool containers ever started: Suricata, Zeek, Arkime, OpenSearch, WireGuard, OpenVPN) — openvpn specifically with --profile manual, since its service is profile-gated. Does NOT remove the 'opensmart' Docker network, container images, or bind-mounted application data (SQLite DBs, logs). Full command output goes to logs/uninstall.log.

integrity_check.description: Shared by start's container path, restart, and recreate.
steps: Wait for the container to reach a stable running state (same crash-loop-tolerant stability check install uses)
Poll /api/health on the container's published port (resolved via docker port, not assumed) for up to 5 minutes — a cold start needs to uv sync/npm install/npm run build inside the container first
Check every ancestor directory of the checkout is traversable by the container's non-root user (fails clearly here — e.g. installing under /root, mode 700 — instead of an opaque crash loop later)
Install Docker Engine + Compose plugin if not already present
Create the external 'opensmart' bridge network (172.250.250.0/24) idempotently

chown -R 1000:1000 the whole repo (container runs as non-root uid 1000; a root-owned checkout otherwise breaks .venv/node_modules/DB creation); also registers this checkout as a git safe.directory in root's global gitconfig, since the chown is exactly what makes a later 'git pull' (typically run as root, to fetch updates) fail with 'detected dubious ownership' otherwise
docker compose up -d in opensmart/containers/run/opensmart/ (command: ./opensmart.sh start --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 --prod)
Poll for a stable running container (not just a brief window between crash-loop restarts)
Poll container logs for the first-run admin password and print it on the host
install.verification_status: Verified against a real Docker Engine on Debian 13. Hardening from that verification: bind-mount ownership handling, a sufficiently long install-time password-reveal timeout, and a pre-flight check for a related crash loop (container's own entrypoint gets 'Permission denied' — chowning the checkout doesn't help when an ANCESTOR directory like /root, mode 700, blocks the non-root container user's traversal) (see steps above) rather than a silent chown. Also: a host with unreliable network access to PyPI/npm can crash-loop for well past the 5-minute password-reveal window, and install used to print an unconditional '✔ running' banner regardless of whether that wait actually succeeded — fixed so the final banner (and exit code) reflects whether readiness was actually confirmed.

output.terminal: One line per main step (10 total: root check, path-traversability check, distro detection, Docker Engine install, network creation, image build, ownership fix, container start, stability check, readiness/password wait), preceded by a banner (ASCII honeycomb logo, Mizton Labs & Honeynet Mexico Team attribution). Raw command output (apt-get, docker build, docker compose) is not printed to the terminal.
output.log_file: logs/install.log — created fresh on every run, holds full timestamped step markers plus all redirected command output. On failure, the terminal step line is closed with 'failed' and points at this log.

stop.action: docker compose stop in opensmart/containers/run/opensmart/ — stops the container without removing it (docker compose start brings it back). No-op with a clear message if the container doesn't exist or is already stopped.

reports: Container state via docker inspect: State.Status (running/restarting/exited/...) and RestartCount

Application health, only checked when the container is running: curl against http://localhost:<published-port>/api/health, port resolved via docker port rather than assumed — distinguishes a running-but-unreachable container (still starting or crashed) from a genuinely healthy one

version.output: OpenSMART <major version> (commit <short git sha>) — major version is the hardcoded VERSION_MAJOR constant near the top of opensmart.sh (currently v0.3, no 'beta' suffix — distinct from the 'v0.3 beta' identifier used elsewhere, e.g. config.py's APP_VERSION default and the README title), commit is `git rev-parse --short HEAD` resolved from ROOT_DIR (falls back to 'unknown' outside a git checkout).

reset_and_health.action: Forwards to opensmart/scripts/run_app.sh's own subcommand of the same name — inside the 'opensmart' container (docker exec) if one exists, or directly on the host otherwise. Always passes -i; adds -t too, but only when opensmart.sh's own stdin is a real terminal ([[ -t 0 ]]). Also passes RUN_APP_INVOKE_AS=./opensmart.sh via `docker exec -e` (host-mode invocations inherit it as an exported shell variable instead) so run_app.sh's own 'Run ... to do X' messages say './opensmart.sh' instead of naming itself.
reset_and_health.fixed: bash's `read -p` only prints a prompt when stdin is an actual tty. docker exec -i (no -t) keeps stdin open for input but allocates no pseudo-TTY, so the reset-* confirmation prompt was silently invisible (though still functionally read) when going through the container — this is what the conditional -t fixes. A second issue fixed at the same time: run_app.sh's post-action messages (e.g. 'Run ./scripts/run_app.sh start to start OpenSMART.') always named itself even when invoked through the opensmart.sh wrapper, which was confusing since that path doesn't exist as a user-facing command of opensmart.sh — RUN_APP_INVOKE_AS makes these messages reference whichever entrypoint was actually used.

image.name: opensmart/web
image.hardening: No baked-in password and no sudo for the 'opensmart' Linux user — docker exec doesn't require a Linux password, and nothing in 'start --prod' needs root.
image.mount: opensmart/ directory bind-mounted at the same absolute path inside the container as on the host (host-path parity via OPENSMART_PROJECT_DIR, not a fixed /opt path), not copied into the image, so container behavior reflects live host source.
image.python: ENV UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system forces uv to use the apt-installed python3 (already 3.13.x on Debian 13) instead of also downloading its own managed Python build from astral's CDN on every cold start — a second, avoidable network dependency on top of the actual package installs (fastapi/uvicorn/etc. via PyPI, which this does NOT eliminate). Cold starts were crash-looping with '[FAIL] Python 3.13 available (not found via uv)' on a network with unreliable egress to astral's CDN.
image.uv_cache: UV_CACHE_DIR is set (in opensmart/containers/run/opensmart/docker-compose.yml) to .uv-cache/ inside the already bind-mounted project directory, instead of uv's default location in the container's own ephemeral home directory. No separate volume mount needed — it's already covered by the project's host-path-parity mount. This means a successful backend package sync persists on the host and survives container recreation, so a flaky network only has to cooperate once rather than on every recreate/reinstall. Package sync (fastapi/uvicorn/etc. via PyPI) stalled repeatedly on a fresh .venv even after the python-interpreter fix above, since each container recreation previously started with a cold cache.

app_script.description: The actual host-process launcher — what opensmart.sh's non-container path (and the container's own entrypoint, via opensmart.sh start --prod) delegates to. Has its own consistent subcommand CLI, mirroring opensmart.sh's: start, stop, status, restart, reset-admin-password, reset-data-all, reset-data-ids, reset-data-network, reset-all, health. No default command — a bare invocation with no subcommand now errors with usage, matching opensmart.sh's own behavior (this used to implicitly mean 'start'; that implicit default was removed for consistency).

commands.start: start [--host H] [--port P] [--prod] — same behavior as before (dev servers or single --prod process), now also writes logs/run_app.state (PID/HOST/PORT/PROD) once the backend is confirmed alive.
commands.stop: Reads logs/run_app.state; if the recorded PID is alive, SIGTERM (SIGKILL after a 15s grace period), then removes the state file. No-op with a message if nothing is running.
commands.status: Reads logs/run_app.state; if the recorded PID is alive, reports it plus curl's /api/health on the recorded host:port. Reports 'not running' otherwise.
commands.restart: Reuses the previous --host/--port/--prod from logs/run_app.state unless explicitly overridden on the command line, stops the existing instance, then falls through into the same code path as start.
commands.reset_and_health: reset-admin-password / reset-data-all / reset-data-ids / reset-data-network / reset-all / health — unchanged behavior from before, just renamed from --flag form to subcommand form (e.g. --reset-admin-password -> reset-admin-password).

app_script.invoke_as_self_reference: RUN_APP_INVOKE_AS (env var, defaults to './opensmart/scripts/run_app.sh') controls how run_app.sh refers to itself in messages like 'Run <X> start to start OpenSMART.' and 'Run <X> health for a full diagnostic report.'. opensmart.sh exports it as './opensmart.sh' before invoking run_app.sh (host mode) and passes it via `docker exec -e` (container mode), so these messages point at whichever entrypoint the operator actually used instead of always naming run_app.sh.
app_script.state_file: logs/run_app.state (relative to the app dir, i.e. opensmart/logs/run_app.state) — plain KEY=VALUE lines (PID, HOST, PORT, PROD). Read via a small grep/cut helper, not `source`, to avoid executing file content.
app_script.known_bug_fixed: cleanup() (the EXIT/INT/TERM trap) used to unconditionally rm the state file on every invocation's exit, including read-only status/stop/health calls from a SEPARATE process — so running `status` while a different instance was live would wipe that instance's state file, making the next status/stop/restart call incorrectly report 'not running'. Fixed by only touching the state file when BACKEND_PID is set (i.e. only the invocation that actually started a backend owns and cleans up the file). Verified with a full start -> status (x2) -> restart -> stop cycle against a real running instance.

dev_commands.frontend_install_dev: cd opensmart/frontend && npm install && npm run dev
dev_commands.backend_import_check: cd opensmart && uv run --project backend --python 3.13 python -c "import backend.app.admin_tools; import backend.app.main; print('backend imports ok')"
dev_commands.known_gotcha: opensmart/backend/.venv's console-script shebangs (uvicorn, etc.) are absolute paths. Any time the app directory is renamed or moved, delete and resync: rm -rf opensmart/backend/.venv && cd opensmart && uv sync --project backend --python 3.13. A bare 'python -c ...' import check still works on a stale venv — only console-script entry points break — so it is not a reliable health check by itself.

summary: Argon2 password hashing (argon2-cffi); plaintext passwords never stored
Server-side sessions in SQLite, HTTP-only cookie, SameSite=Lax
CSRF token required on mutating authenticated requests
Failed-login lockout tracked by username + client IP
Shell hooks run via subprocess.run([...], shell=False) only
Configurable password complexity policy (strict/moderate/low/disabled), enforced server-side
Forced password change (must_change_password) after any admin/CLI-triggered reset, enforced server-side (423 on all but a small exempt set of routes) not just in the UI
Container provisioning goes through a restricted docker-socket-proxy allowlist (CONTAINERS/NETWORKS/IMAGES/VOLUMES/POST only), never a direct docker.sock mount into the app container
current_limitations: No Secure cookie flag — production behind HTTPS should add it
X-Forwarded-For trusted unconditionally — restrict to known reverse proxies in production
Module config accepted as raw JSON string without content validation
Uploaded logos stored as data URLs in SQLite — keep image sizes modest

docker-socket-proxy allowlist still grants POST on CONTAINERS/IMAGES/NETWORKS/VOLUMES — a compromised backend could create/remove containers or pull arbitrary images through it, though not exec into other containers, build images, or touch Swarm/host-level Docker state
Container provisioning calls are not serialized per-container; concurrent overlapping start/stop requests are untested

phases.name: Password policy, first-run Wizard, Network IDS source toggle, container provisioning engine
phases.status: done, verified against a real Docker Engine
phases.summary: Password: must_change_password enforced server-side (423 outside a small exempt route set) plus a configurable strict/moderate/low/disabled complexity policy; the two previously-duplicated password-hashing code paths are now one shared helper. Wizard: 5-step first-run flow (update ack, logo, modules, tools, finish) gated by a wizard_completed setting that defaults true for existing installs. Network IDS: eve_source toggle (external, default / native, auto-derived path). Provisioning: containers/run/ moved from the repo root into opensmart/containers/run/ (containers/build/ stays at the repo root as build-time templates); main app container mount switched from a fixed /opt/opensmart path to host-path parity via OPENSMART_PROJECT_DIR (exported by opensmart.sh); a docker-socket-proxy sidecar (restricted allowlist: CONTAINERS/NETWORKS/IMAGES/VOLUMES/POST only) replaces a direct docker.sock mount; backend app/provisioning.py shells out to `docker compose` against it to start/stop Suricata/Zeek/Arkime/OpenSearch/WireGuard/OpenVPN, wired into the Wizard's Finish step and the Network IDS native-Suricata toggle. Wazuh and Graylog have no container template yet, so modules/tools backed by them report 'no template available' rather than silently no-op'ing. Verified end-to-end against a real Docker Engine: built images, started/stopped Suricata through the API with docker ps confirming actual state. Bugs found and fixed through live testing: an app-container self-reference loop once it gained Docker access, a mount anchored one directory too deep, and a too-narrow proxy allowlist (docker compose needs /volumes even for bind-mount-only projects).

phases.name: Wizard redesign, real Status, themes, VPN module
phases.status: done, verified against a real Docker Engine
phases.summary: Status: container_overview() derives per-container status/image/uptime/restarts/health warnings from `docker inspect` (EXEC is proxy-blocked), with per-project restart from the Status page; placeholders remain only for Honeypot/LXC Manager/Graylog/NTOP. Wizard: rebuilt as 4 steps (Basics: app name+logo; Network: real host NICs via a one-off busybox run on the host network, persisted as monitor_interfaces and injected into Suricata as CAPTURE_IFACES for multi-interface capture; Modules & Tools: recommended defaults pre-selected with dependency auto-enable notices, Wazuh/Arkime iframe URLs prefilled; Provision: sequential runner with phases, progress bar, per-service container-level results and a final info/warning/error summary). Themes: all styles.css color literals tokenized into CSS variables with generated Dark (default)/Classic (light)/Matrix palettes, persisted in the theme setting and applied pre-login. VPN: full instance manager (backend/app/vpn.py, vpn_instances table) — OpenVPN or WireGuard instances as generated compose projects each on its own UDP port and unique 10.<n>.0.0/24 subnet, easy-rsa/wg key material produced by one-off containers through the socket proxy, user lifecycle (create with downloadable client config, expiry visible, revoke via CRL/peer removal), optional OpenVPN LDAP/Samba auth via openvpn-auth-ldap. Wazuh gained a real container template (official v4.14.6 images, indexer remapped to 9201). Fixed en route: native-Suricata eve.json path ignored by the ingestion engine (eve_source now resolved centrally by eve_ingest.resolve_eve_json_path), Arkime /data permissions under unprivileged UID mapping (init-data-dir one-off), and VPN key files unreadable across UID mappings (keys via stdout / chmod a+rwX after PKI mutations).

known_limitations: Placeholder module/tool pages remain only for Honeypot, LXC Manager, Graylog and NTOP; everything else shows real container-derived state
No automated tests beyond syntax/import/build checks
Frontend dependency versions use broad ('latest') ranges; package-lock.json is tracked for reproducibility
No container template exists yet for Graylog — the tool reports 'no template available' when provisioning is attempted
OpenVPN instances need /dev/net/tun on the Docker host (LXC hosts must pass it through); starting one without it fails with a clear daemon error surfaced in the UI

The /proxmox and /opnsense front-door aliases are best-effort: those apps have no native base-path support, so subpath proxying can break consoles/websockets/absolute assets. Use direct url:port mode for full fidelity. Arkime and Wazuh aliases are reliable (they support base paths).

Front-door tool aliases (relative paths like /arkime/) only resolve when OpenSMART is reached through the proxy port (default :8080); accessed directly on :8000 they 404 — use direct url:port mode there.
Wazuh containers ship with upstream demo credentials (flagged in their compose file) — rotate before real use
The Wazuh-backed modules (Threat Detection Alerts, Endpoint, Vulnerability Management) provision and monitor the containers but do not yet ingest Wazuh data into OpenSMART pages
WireGuard peer changes restart the instance (wg-quick re-reads its config only on start)
